experiment_data.hypothesis: Per-DOF inverse-variance weighted loss will improve CRM by prioritizing high-precision DOFs (rotation/gripper), compared to uniform MSE
experiment_data.notes:
Training completed successfully (50/50 epochs, EXIT_CODE=0), val_loss continuously improved through final epoch.

Per-DOF weighted val_loss=0.000124 vs MSE baseline val_loss=0.002080. CAVEAT: loss values are NOT directly comparable — perdof_weighted uses inverse-variance weighting (range 0.0107–3.7318, ~350x) which rescales the loss function. The low numerical loss reflects that the model fits high-precision DOFs (rotation/gripper, weight up to 3.73x) very well, while de-emphasizing high-variance DOFs (translation, weight as low as 0.01x).

All 4 variants completed on same data/architecture:
- mse: val_loss=0.002080
- perdof_weighted: val_loss=0.000124
- conformal_guided: val_loss=0.013343
- combined: still running (epoch 48, val_loss=0.005302)

Definitive comparison requires downstream robot evaluation (success rate) with each checkpoint. The per-DOF weighting approach shows excellent convergence and the model prioritizes rotation/gripper precision as designed.
